selection_rationale: Select cand-gnr-001 (GVR-ProtocolEval) because it directly targets the core track mandate—empirically measuring generate–validate–repair (GVR) impact on operational failures across protocols and modalities—has strong falsifiability and venue relevance, and is supported by the candidate's cited novelty/feasibility evidence (see evidence_record_ids). Reviewer verdict: pass. The required design repairs are implementable prior to preregistration and will materially strengthen internal and construct validity.
unresolved_uncertainties: UQ1: To what extent do LLM-generated network configurations, validated by current prototype verifier pipelines, prevent operational failures (reachability loss, policy violation) in realistic heterogeneous environments? (evidence refs: https://openalex.org/W4411109869, https://openalex.org/W4399629579)

UQ2: How effective are generate–validate–repair pipelines across diverse network protocols, vendor syntaxes, and interaction modalities (API vs. CLI), and what are their residual failure modes? (evidence refs: https://openalex.org/W4399629579, https://openalex.org/W7141772527)
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Increase fidelity of vendor-syntax emulation (sample real device snippets or vendor templates) and document limits.
Preregister the deterministic verifier rule set, provide quantitative coverage/limitations, and include unit tests for verifier behaviors.
Provide power/sample-size calculations for protocol/modality subgroups and adjust the task bank accordingly.
Specify seed/control for model nondeterminism, define retry policy, and log all reruns (preregister nondeterminism controls).
